description: Phase-RAG — auto-adaptive Tool-RAG eval harness. Lands BEFORE bulk MCP roundup so we validate retrieval quality on the known native tool baseline first, then catch regressions when MCPs swamp the index. Plan doc: docs/tool-rag-eval-plan-2026-05-20.md. Key resource: D:/tmp/bench_dataset.json (188 production query→tool pairs mined from real conversations, 47% IT / 53% EN) is the Layer-1 seed — copy in + sanitize, don't hand-author. 3 stories with intentional ordering: A01 (promote dataset + Layer-2 autogen-from-examples + alias map) → A02 (vector-path eval + Layer-3 distractor stress + sunset old fixture) → A03 (mining pipeline + external benchmark fetcher + CI gate). NO LLM-as-judge in v1 (Layer 5 future). NO production-mining auto-schedule in v1 (manual via cmd helper). Master HEAD at queue creation: TBD post-Wave3. STRICT one-story-exit per scripts/ralph/CLAUDE.md.

userStories.title: Promote bench_mined.json + alias map + Layer-2 autogen-from-examples
userStories.description: Bootstrap the auto-adaptive eval foundation: (a) sanitize-and-promote D:/tmp/bench_dataset.json into the repo as the Layer-1 production-mined fixture; (b) add an alias map for legacy tool-name → current registry-name; (c) add a Layer-2 autogen that derives ≥3 eval queries per native tool from its description + examples — covers new MCPs before they have production traces. (a) SANITIZE+COPY: read D:/tmp/bench_dataset.json (188 entries). Run regex sanitization on every `query` string: strip emails (\b[A-Z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Z0-9.-]+\.[A-Z]{2,}\b case-insensitive), strip phone-like sequences (\b\+?\d[\d -]{6,}\d\b), strip long opaque hex tokens (\b[A-Fa-f0-9]{32,}\b), replace numeric chat_id with literal '<chat>' before write. Strip `chat_id` + `turn_index` fields entirely from the output (telemetry, not eval data). Write the cleaned JSON to internal/agent/tools/index/testdata/bench_mined.json. (b) ALIAS MAP: new file internal/agent/tools/index/alias_map.go (~50 LOC) exporting `var LegacyToolNameAliases = map[string]string{...}` covering the legacy sub-action names observed in the dataset → current registry names: read_file→file (with action=read), write_file→file (action=write), search_files→file (action=search), apply_patch→file (action=patch), list_files→file (action=list), read_source→source (action=read), lint_sources→source (action=lint), read_tool→dev_tool (action=read), and the few mcp_* names that survived a rename. Function `ResolveAlias(name string) (canonical string, action string)` returns the modern tool name + optional action sub-tag (empty action means no sub-routing). (c) QUALITY CLASSIFIER: new file internal/agent/tools/index/eval_classifier.go (~100 LOC). Function `Classify(entry MinedEntry) Quality` returns one of `QualityClean | QualityAmbiguous | QualityMulti` using these heuristics: QualityMulti = len(entry.Tools) > 1; QualityAmbiguous = NOT QualityMulti AND (len(query rune count) < 10 OR query matches /^(che palle|guarda adesso|si|no|ok|prova|ciao|aura)$/i — short single-word/short-imperative without explicit object); QualityClean = everything else. The eval scoring DIFFERENTIATES: Clean queries scored at precision@1 + hit@3; Ambiguous queries scored only at hit@5 (forgiving); Multi queries scored as `any expected tool in top-K`. Embed the Quality field at parse time so consumers don't re-classify. Test `TestClassifier_KnownEntries` with ~20 representative entries from the dataset asserts expected classification. (d) LAYER-2 AUTOGEN: new file internal/agent/tools/index/eval_autogen.go (~150 LOC). Function `AutoGenerateQueries(reg *tools.Registry) []EvalEntry` iterates all registered tool defs and for each tool produces ≥3 query entries: (i) direct = ToolDefinition.Description (truncated to first sentence), (ii) tool-name-masked = direct with the tool name + its tokenized parts regexed-out (e.g. for `search_memory` the regex /\b(search|memory|search_memory)\b/i), (iii) italian-paraphrase = lookup in the translation cache keyed by SHA-256(direct). For each example in ToolDefinition.Examples, also generate a direct+masked+IT triplet from `example.Description`. Caveat: skip the IT triplet when the translation cache doesn't have the key — emit a t.Logf warning naming the missing key so the operator knows to run cmd/eval_translate. (e) TRANSLATION CACHE: new file internal/agent/tools/index/testdata/eval_autogen_translations.json. Schema: `{ "<sha256 of EN string>": {"en": "<original>", "it": "<italian>"} }`. Bootstrap with ~50 entries covering the 14 current native tools' descriptions + their example descriptions. Hand-author the v1 cache (it's small and the user wants high quality on the seed). cmd/eval_translate (US-RAG-A03) regenerates additions automatically. (f) COVERAGE TEST: new function `TestFixtureCoversAllTools` in internal/agent/tools/index/eval_topk_test.go asserts every name in `buildEvalRegistry().AllToolNames()` (or equivalent) has ≥3 entries in the merged Layer-1 + Layer-2 fixture. Fail with a clear message listing tools below the threshold. (g) BACKWARD COMPAT: keep internal/agent/tools/index/eval_topk_fixture.json in place for this story — A02 deletes it. The existing TestDiscoveryTopKEval continues to pass against the legacy fixture (regression guard) AND the new TestFixtureCoversAllTools runs against the new merged source.

userStories.title: Vector-path eval + Layer-3 distractor stress + sunset legacy fixture
userStories.description: Two production hardenings: the vector path (today's prod retrieval) gets eval coverage for the first time, and we add the MCP-Bench-style distractor stress that future-proofs against the MCP roundup. (a) VECTOR EVAL: new file internal/agent/tools/index/eval_vector_test.go (~250 LOC). Function `TestVectorTopKEval(t *testing.T)` mirrors TestDiscoveryTopKEval but drives `ToolVectorIndex.Search(ctx, query, topK)` against a live Qdrant + embeddinggemma sidecar setup. Gate via env probe: if AURA_QDRANT_URL or POCKETTTS-style sidecar URLs are unset OR /health returns non-200, SKIP with logged reason (not FAIL). This matches the existing AURA_SKIP_TOOL_EVALS=1 pattern. Use the merged Layer-1 + Layer-2 fixture from A01 (NOT the legacy file). Assertions: global hit@3 >= 75%; per-category breakdown (memory tools >= 80%, web tools >= 80%, files tools >= 70%, exec tools >= 70%, system tools >= 80% — categories derived from a small static categoryOf(toolName) function in eval_vector_test.go); p95 latency < 200ms (per memory budget feedback_minillm_cpu_not_viable_for_tool_retrieval); MRR computed + logged but not gated in v1. (b) DISTRACTOR STRESS: new file internal/agent/tools/index/eval_distractor.go (~100 LOC). Function `InjectDistractors(reg *tools.Registry, distractors []DistractorTool, seed int64) *tools.Registry` returns a new registry with the input tools + N distractors (where N = len(distractors), default 100). DistractorTool implements tools.Tool with hand-templated Name+Description that look real but don't overlap with current tool names — function checks `reg.HasName(distractor.Name)` and re-rolls (sha256 of the seed for determinism) on collision. New testdata/distractors.json with 100 synthetic distractors covering plausible MCP domains (calendar_event_create, github_pr_review, kimai_timer_start, vikunja_task_complete, ...) — these are pure synthetic templates, NOT real MCP tools we plan to adopt (avoid future name collisions). (c) DISTRACTOR ASSERTIONS: both TestDiscoveryTopKEval AND TestVectorTopKEval gain a `_WithDistractors` variant that runs the same fixture through the registry+distractors. Per-tool robustness score = (hit@3 with distractors) / (hit@3 without distractors). Threshold: every tool robustness >= 60%; below that, log with name+score for description-rework signal. Tests fail if ANY tool drops below 50% (hard floor — that's a description-quality bug, not noise). (d) LEGACY FIXTURE SUNSET: DELETE internal/agent/tools/index/eval_topk_fixture.json. Update TestDiscoveryTopKEval to read from the merged Layer-1 + Layer-2 source instead. Old `evalEntry` type can stay (it's compatible) — just change the file path + add the Quality-aware scoring. (e) METRICS PRINTING: when a test reports a miss or below-threshold result, the t.Logf message includes the FULL top-K with scores so the operator can diagnose without re-running. Format: `MISS query=... lang=it quality=clean expected=search_memory got=[web:0.42, dev_tool:0.38, ...]`.

userStories.notes: GROUND-TRUTH BEFORE EDIT: (1) Read internal/agent/tools/registry/registry_search_vector.go IN FULL to understand ToolVectorIndex.Search signature + the Qdrant client wiring. (2) Read internal/agent/tools/index/eval_topk_test.go AGAIN — the new tests mirror its structure exactly. (3) Read internal/agent/tools/index/reconciler.go (the boot-side that upserts tool embeddings into Qdrant) to know what shape the index expects. The eval test needs to: instantiate a ToolVectorIndex, ensure the registry's tools are upserted into the test collection, run Search. The reconciler is the upsert path — call it or replicate it. (4) Read compose.yaml to confirm sidecar URLs the test will read from env. SIDECAR SKIP DISCIPLINE: env probe goes at the top of TestVectorTopKEval: `if os.Getenv("AURA_QDRANT_URL") == "" { t.Skip("AURA_QDRANT_URL not set — vector path eval skipped") }`. Same for embedding endpoint. The test must run in CI without these sidecars without failing the suite — skip is mandatory, no FAILURE for unconfigured environments. DISTRACTOR NAMING: the 100 synthetic distractors should LOOK like plausible MCP tools (mcp_<service>_<action>) but use service names we'll never adopt (e.g. mcp_acme_widget_get) — that way when future real MCP names land, there's no collision. Pre-fix with `mcp_distractor_` as a safety net. Document this naming convention in distractors.json header comment + in the eval_distractor.go file. SEED DETERMINISM: the distractor sampling uses a seed (env AURA_EVAL_SEED, default 42) so CI runs are reproducible. Different seeds for ad-hoc operator runs are OK; default tests must be deterministic. PER-CATEGORY THRESHOLDS: hard-code a small map[string]float64 like `var perCategoryThreshold = map[string]float64{"memory":0.80, "web":0.80, "files":0.70, "exec":0.70, "system":0.80}`. Function `categoryOf(toolName string) string` does a switch on tool name prefix or suffix to assign. Document the mapping in a comment block. ROBUSTNESS SCORE: only meaningful on Clean queries (Ambiguous + Multi are noisy by construction); compute over Clean subset only. P95 LATENCY: capture per-query duration in a slice, sort, take the 95th-percentile element. Don't import a stats library — 8 lines of stdlib suffice. SCOPE DISCIPLINE: NO mining-pipeline cmd in this story — that's A03. NO external benchmark fetcher — that's A03. NO dashboard panel — that's a future follow-up. INVARIANT: the lexical-path TestDiscoveryTopKEval continues to pass — vector path is additive, not replacement. Both paths matter (lexical is the fallback when Qdrant is down).

userStories.title: Mining pipeline + external benchmark fetcher + CI gate (cmd/probe_tool_rag)
userStories.description: Three operator-facing binaries that close the auto-adaptive loop: re-mine production data when the user wants a fresh dataset, fetch external benchmarks for cross-MCP coverage, and run the full eval suite from one binary with metrics + exit code suitable for CI. (a) MINING PIPELINE: new cmd/eval_mine_conversations/main.go (~140 LOC). Reads from Aura's live SQLite `conversations` table (path: DB_PATH env, default ./aura.db). SQL: `SELECT user_text, tool_calls_json, succeeded_at FROM conversations WHERE tool_calls_json IS NOT NULL AND user_text IS NOT NULL`. For each row, parse the tool_calls_json (it's the existing archive JSON shape — verify with grep `tool_calls` internal/conversation/archive.go before writing the SQL). Extract `(query, []toolName)` pairs. Apply the same sanitization regex as A01. Apply the same Classifier from A01. Deduplicate by SHA-256 of normalized query. Emit JSON to a path passed via -out flag (default: stdout). Setting gate: refuses to run unless `TOOL_RAG_EVAL_MINING=true` env is set (privacy guard — Davide's chats are private). Document the mining frequency in a comment: 'Run weekly as the conversation archive grows; check the diff before promoting to testdata/bench_mined.json.' (b) EXTERNAL FETCHER: new cmd/eval_fetch_external/main.go (~180 LOC). Fetches public artifacts for three datasets: HumanMCP, MCP-Bench, MCP-Atlas (in that order — HumanMCP largest, most natural queries). For each, the fetcher needs the actual artifact URL — the paper page links to a HuggingFace dataset or a GitHub release. The fetcher implementation includes a small registry of dataset URLs + parsers (one per dataset) with a clear `TODO: URL needs verification 2026-06` comment so a future iter can update if a redirect changes. Pull, parse to a normalized {query, expected_tools[], source_dataset, source_lang} shape, filter to entries whose expected_tool overlaps with Aura's Registry.AllToolNames() (post-alias-resolution from A01). Cache to internal/agent/tools/index/testdata/external_eval_cache.json (GITIGNORED — add to .gitignore in this commit). (c) UNIFIED PROBE: new cmd/probe_tool_rag/main.go (~140 LOC). Single binary that: loads Layer-1 (bench_mined.json) + Layer-2 (autogen) + Layer-4 (external cache if present); runs both lexical + vector paths; prints a table with global + per-category precision@1, hit@3, hit@5, MRR, p50/p95 latency; exits 0 if all thresholds met OR 1 with a per-tool/per-category breakdown of misses. Output format: machine-readable JSON to stdout when -json flag, human table by default. Flags: -lexical-only, -vector-only, -tts (no — that's other probe), -k 5 (override topK), -threshold 0.75 (override global gate), -seed (for distractor reproducibility). (d) MAKEFILE TARGET: add `tool-rag-eval` target to the project Makefile (or create one if missing — grep first). Invokes `go run ./cmd/probe_tool_rag -threshold 0.75`. (e) CI INVOCATION: extend .github/workflows/ci.yml (or wherever CI lives — grep) with an opt-in step `if env.AURA_RUN_TOOL_RAG == 'true'` that runs `make tool-rag-eval`. Default OFF — runs only when manually enabled (sidecars + cache prep cost). (f) DOC: a small docs/tool-rag-eval-runbook.md (NEW, ~80 lines) explaining the three binaries, when to refresh each input, how to interpret the report, where the thresholds live, how to update the alias map when a tool is renamed.

userStories.notes: GROUND-TRUTH BEFORE EDIT: (1) Grep for the conversations archive write path: `grep -rn 'INSERT INTO conversations' internal/conversation/` — find the JSON shape that tool_calls_json carries, write the SELECT to match. (2) Find Aura's existing Makefile (or absence): `ls Makefile` — if absent, create a minimal one with at least the tool-rag-eval target. (3) Find CI workflow: `ls .github/workflows/` — extend the existing file rather than creating a new one. (4) Read cmd/probe_chat/main.go for the flag-handling pattern Aura uses — match that style (flag pkg, env fallbacks, structured logging). EXTERNAL FETCHER URL DISCIPLINE: paper arxiv URLs are stable but the actual dataset artifacts often live on HuggingFace or GitHub releases. For each dataset, write a brief block comment with the paper URL + the artifact URL you used + the date you fetched. If the artifact URL is dead, log an error with the paper URL so a future iter can re-find. DON'T HARDCODE the dataset in this commit — keep the fetcher as a fetch-and-write tool with the URLs in constants; the actual cache file is gitignored and generated on demand. If 1-2 fetcher targets fail (404, paywall, etc.), the binary should still succeed for the working datasets — partial success is fine. PROBE OUTPUT QUALITY: the default human-readable table is what an operator will see most. Use the format: `Category | hit@3 | precision@1 | MRR | p95ms | Status` rows; bottom-line `Global hit@3: 78.4% (gate 75.0%) — PASS`. Color codes ONLY if stdout.IsTerminal (no ANSI escapes leaking into CI logs). SETTING-GATE EXAMPLE: in cmd/eval_mine_conversations/main.go top: `if os.Getenv("TOOL_RAG_EVAL_MINING") != "true" { log.Fatal("TOOL_RAG_EVAL_MINING must be set to true — this mines real conversations and the operator must opt in explicitly") }`. Document this in the runbook. ALIAS-MAP REUSE: cmd/eval_mine_conversations + cmd/eval_fetch_external both consume the alias map from A01 — import it as a library function, don't duplicate the map. SCOPE DISCIPLINE: NO dashboard panel in this story — that's a follow-up. NO LLM-as-judge — out of v1. NO scheduled cron for the mining pipeline — manual via cmd. The runbook documents the manual cadence. INVARIANT: if the external fetcher hits 404s or rate-limits, the rest of the eval still runs against Layer 1+2 only — partial coverage is fine. The CI gate must not break when external benchmarks can't be fetched.
